guitar.notes: Michael Romeo has a well-documented signature Caparison Dellinger model, well known in prog-metal circles.

tone.target: modern high-gain metal with tight low end and mid bite
tone.profile: modern high-gain metal with tight low end and mid bite
tone.summary: Gate 1 -> OD 9 -> Distortion (Chief/RAT) -> Recti Amp -> UK Vintage 4x12 -> Guitar EQ 2 -> Chorus -> Digital Delay

rig.name: Symphony X - Set The World On Fire - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Eliminate hum and background noise for tight recording.
Provide aggressive mid-range boost and tighten the low end for palm muting.
blocks.gap: The OD 9 is used as a pre-gain booster rather than a traditional dirt pedal, focusing on harmonic enhancement.

blocks.purpose: Achieve dense saturation and aggressive mid-range bite required for modern metal.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style model is chosen for its punchy, focused mids, avoiding the scoop of Muff or the fuzziness of Red Haze.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the high-gain, tight response of a Mesa/Rectifier-style amp.
Provide a robust and articulate platform for the high-gain tone.
Focus the upper mids and tighten the low end while maintaining clarity.
blocks.gap: Using EQ 2 allows for more precise mid-range sculpting than a single band boost.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle width and movement to the overall tone without losing aggression.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used subtly here, as heavy modulation would clash with the aggressive metal tone.

blocks.purpose: Add rhythmic depth and space to the performance.
Provide a subtle sense of space without muddying the high-gain tone.
blocks.gap: The mix is kept very low to ensure the metal aggression remains paramount.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism with a dedicated IR for better low-end definition and mid-range focus.

proposals.reason: Enhance tightness, low-end punch, and mid-focus for modern metal.
